Haemoperfusion involves the passage of blood through an adsorbent material such as activated char- coal or synthetic hydrophobic polystyrene resins that can re- tain certain drugs and toxic agents. Early problems with char- coal haemoperfusion such as charcoal embolism, marked thrombocytopenia, fibrinogen loss, and pyrogen reactions have been largely overcome by purification procedures and by coating the carbon with biocompatible polymers. Howev- er, transient falls in platelet count, leucocyte count, and circu- latory concentrations of clotting factors, calcium, glucose, urea, creatinine, and urate have been reported during haemo- perfusion.
